title: Cost Management capabilities and tags
learningObjective: Describe Cost Management capabilities (cost analysis, budgets, alerts, recommendations) and use tags to organise and report resources.
foundation: Microsoft Cost Management shows what you've spent, where and why, and helps you control it: cost analysis reports, budgets, alerts and savings recommendations.

A budget is a spending limit you set (for example $2,000 a month for a subscription). Azure alerts you when spend or forecast reaches a threshold. Budgets don't stop resources by themselves, but they can trigger automation.
Tags are name/value labels you add to resources, such as dept=finance or env=prod. They help you find, organise and report on resources, especially costs.
engineer: Cost analysis: explore actual and forecast costs by service, resource, resource group, location, meter or tag; save views; export data to storage on a schedule.

Cost alerts: budget alerts (when spend or forecast reaches a threshold), credit alerts (Azure Prepayment consumption), department spending quota alerts (EA), and anomaly alerts. Budgets can trigger action groups (email, runbooks, Logic Apps) to scale down or stop resources.
Recommendations: Azure Advisor cost recommendations appear in Cost Management (resize or shut down underused VMs, buy reservations).

Tags: up to 50 name/value pairs per resource, resource group or subscription. Uses: resource management (find and act on resources by tag), cost management and optimisation (group costs), operations (criticality, SLA), security (data classification), governance and compliance, workload optimisation and automation (for example shut down VMs tagged schedule=office-hours).

Tags aren't inherited by resources from their resource group or subscription by default. Use Azure Policy (for example 'Inherit a tag from the resource group if missing' or 'Require a tag') or Cost Management tag inheritance (for supported billing accounts) to apply them consistently. Not every resource type supports tags.

animation.caption: See whether VM costs show under the department tag, then pick the right Cost Management tool.

example.title: Chargeback by department
body: Finance asks each department to pay for its own Azure usage. IT requires a dept tag on every resource group with Azure Policy, and adds 'Inherit a tag from the resource group' so new VMs get it automatically.
Cost analysis grouped by dept now shows each department's spend; each department has a monthly budget with alerts at 80% and 100%.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (a free account works)
permissions: Cost Management Contributor for budgets; Tag Contributor or Contributor for tags
limits: Some resource types don't support tags
portal: Cost Management > Cost analysis: Group by Tag.
Policy > Definitions: 'Inherit a tag from the resource group if missing'.
configuration.cli:
az tag update --resource-id <id> --operation Merge --tags dept=finance env=prod
az consumption budget create --budget-name monthly --amount 2000 --time-grain Monthly --start-date 2026-12-01 --end-date 2027-12-01 --category Cost
configuration.powershell:
Update-AzTag -ResourceId <id> -Tag @{dept='finance'} -Operation Merge
New-AzConsumptionBudget -Name monthly -Amount 2000 -TimeGrain Monthly -StartDate 2026-12-01 -Category Cost

Expecting a budget to stop spending by itself
lab.cost: None. The simulation runs entirely in the browser.

troubleshooting.cause: Resources lack the tag; resource group tags aren't inherited.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Azure Policy to require or inherit tags.

troubleshooting.symptom: Budget alert received after spend already exceeded the budget.
troubleshooting.fix: Add forecast-based alerts at lower thresholds.

comparisons.difference: A resource is in one group, but it can have many tags; tags cut across groups and subscriptions.
Budgets alert on spend; Policy controls what can be deployed.

misconceptions.reality: They alert; automation must be added to act.

architectureDecisions: Define a tagging standard (dept, env, owner) and enforce it with Policy.
Set budgets per subscription and department.
